title: "Divergence & the ISS"
subtitle: "Week 1 Thursday · 2 engagement credits"
---

**Standards seeded:** A4, A1 · **You'll need:** your Bring-to-class answers; one laptop per table.

## Opening vote

Question 1 from the reading: identical prompts → identical code? Commit → vote → argue with your table → revote. Then we settle it live: every table sends the *same* projectile prompt to an LLM, and we tally what comes back.

## The class list

Question 2: the program *ran and made a nice plot* — why might it still be wrong? Tables pool their reasons, we build the master list on the board. This list gets photographed and becomes a course artifact; you will be checking your own work against it in week 14.

## The awesome part

Live, from the front: three lines of Python, and the International Space Station's position, speed, and altitude appear. We sanity-check its speed against a 90-minute orbit — your first A1 in the wild. You'll write this program yourself in week 8; today it's here so you know where this course is going.

**Deliverable (2 EC):** your table's contribution to the master list — at least three distinct failure reasons, on the provided card, team names on it.
